state: Sellers control the immediate downside, but frequent alternation prevents a clean trend.
paragraphs: Sellers have immediate command of EURUSD, pressing price down to 1.139 and breaking beneath the latest confirmed low of 1.1455. Confirmed swing structure supports this downside bias with a developing sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Even so, the decline lacks clean execution. Recent downside runs stretch to 6 units in length, but they alternate with sharp counter-moves inside an erratic structural environment. Low opposing wick pressure shows that buyers are offering minimal rejection to the current descent, yet high transition readings indicate that control continues to change hands too easily for this move to qualify as a stable trend.

Looking across the full 104-brick window, market history shows a remarkably balanced distribution between advances and declines, with 53 bullish moves against 51 bearish ones. Average run lengths historically sit very close to each other at 2.52 for buyers and 2.32 for sellers. Recent behavior reveals a sharp departure from that balance. Over the last 12 runs, selling pressure has stretched downward with an average bearish run of 3.5 units while bullish counter-moves have collapsed to an average of just 1.33 units. Sellers are pushing further and lasting longer during their descents, whereas buyers struggle to mount any meaningful follow-through after stepping in.

The descent carries clear force, yet the broader context remains deeply erratic. Continuation scores sit low at 33.7, while transition pressure rests high at 75.3 alongside a chop reading of 94.5. This combination shows that sellers are pushing price downward without establishing orderly control. Re-acceleration ticks up slightly to 17.3, and compression holds steady at 65.8, meaning the volatility range is contracting without signaling fresh expansion behind the move. Price is moving lower inside a transitional background where control shifts repeatedly and timing consistency remains low. The selloff is active, but the underlying structure lacks the clean mechanics required for a stable trend.

The immediate descent rests on harmonic support at 1.139, with deeper downside pivots waiting around 1.136 to 1.1325 and the lower volatility boundary at 1.13458. Overhead, the first test sits inside the 1.14295 to 1.14808 zone, which groups the middle volatility band and the neutral position marker. Reclaiming that area would require buyers to punch through immediate resistance before challenging the broken swing low at 1.1455. Higher up, the falling regression line at 1.16086 marks the larger trend barrier well above current price. That keeps the overarching trend ceiling distant, ensuring that minor bounces face heavy overhead friction even if buyers attempt a temporary recovery.

The selloff can extend further because low opposing wick pressure indicates buyers are offering very little meaningful rejection at current levels. At the same time, the broader volatility envelope remains broad while contracting, meaning price has room to slide further toward the lower boundary at 1.13458 even though fresh volatility is no longer expanding behind the descent. That contracting range acts as a caution instead of a confirmed signal of steady continuation. Meanwhile, a developing bullish Bat pattern sits right at current price around 1.139, offering a source of counter-pressure. This pattern does not reverse the bearish reading on its own, but it introduces friction that could interrupt the decline if sellers fail to maintain their momentum.

The broader market state remains unresolved because high transition pressure and erratic timing keep control unstable. Rapid switching and frequent local flips prevent any clean structural classification. The current bearish lean becomes more convincing only when sellers develop repeated runs with steadier timing and coherent structural progress. That downside bias weakens if buyers gain persistent control, reclaim broken structure near 1.1455, or otherwise invalidate the active sequence. Alternatively, a stable range or orderly directional state can replace the existing disorder without automatically reversing the current downward bias. Until one of those shifts takes hold, the descent operates inside a chaotic transitional background where momentum outpaces stability.
